_provenance.source: Chrome DevTools Protocol driven browser automation against the live BioPrint enrollment page at http://localhost:5173/enroll
_provenance.why_this_matters: This is a real capture from a real browser-automation tool, not a hand-written fixture. It is the strongest single piece of evidence for two design decisions. First, every event carries trusted=true, because CDP input is genuine browser input as far as the page is concerned. Second, navigator.webdriver reports false, so the automation is not self-declaring. A detector built on either flag would have passed this attempt. It was caught on event-ordering forensics instead: the tool fills fields with bulk text insertion, producing input events with no keydown before them, and it teleports the pointer between click targets with no intervening movement.
_provenance.observed_outcome: Rejected at enrollment with the message 'That round looked automated rather than typed.'
_provenance.note: The nonce in this capture is spent and the phrase belongs to an expired challenge, so this file cannot be replayed against a live server. It is retained purely as detector test input.
